dominant_strengths: Clean column rhythm with well-calibrated avatar, name/email stack, and tag chips creating consistent scannable rows
Status pills and department tags use restrained pastel-on-saturated-dot palette that reads quickly without visual noise
Score bars add a useful at-a-glance numeric encoding alongside the digit, doubling channels without clutter
dominant_weaknesses: Highly conventional SaaS directory pattern — nothing structurally novel in layout, sort affordances, or interaction surface
Row-end icon trio (profile, send, kebab) is ambiguous, low-contrast, and crowds the score column without clear hierarchy
Score bar color seems arbitrary (green/blue/orange) without a legend, weakening reflective trust in the metric
fix_priorities: Clarify score color semantics with a tooltip or legend, or unify hue and rely on length
Consolidate trailing actions into a single hover-revealed menu to reduce visual noise per row
Introduce a distinguishing element — density toggle, inline filters, or grouped department headers — to escape template feel
Tighten avatar status-dot contrast and align baseline of multi-line role text with single-line cells
rationale.norman_balance: Behavioral utility leads, visceral polish is competent but generic, and reflective payoff is thin because nothing here will be remembered.
rationale.intent_fit: It is a functioning, legible team directory table that satisfies the brief but does not push the data-table form forward.
